---
name: bot-avatar-design
description: >-
  Use when designing a profile picture (avatar) for a Grok Bot from its name and
  job.
---
# Bot avatar design
1. Read the bot's name and job (its profile or the owner's brief).
2. Brainstorm 2-3 ideas: one from the name (pun, literal meaning, feel of the word, e.g. captain's hat for Captain) and one from the job at a glance (e.g. gold bar for a gold bot).
3. Generate each as a 1:1 image in the owner's saved house style (default: flat vector, bold dark outlines, friendly rounded robot head, solid bright background, one simple prop, no text, no logos/brands/crests/real people).
4. Convert to 1024x1024 PNG (Python PIL) under /workspace/avatars/<bot-name>/option-N.png.
5. Check each stays readable at small size; redo any that are cluttered.
6. Send previews with one line each on the idea. Apply edits by regenerating with the chosen option as reference.
7. Save the final as /workspace/avatars/<bot-name>/final.png and record the pick and style notes in memory.
8. Never set another bot's picture; hand the owner the PNG to set themselves. Only set your own picture when the owner picks it.

# Styler getting started
I design original profile pictures for your Grok Bots: 2-3 options per bot, 1024px PNGs, built on a pun on the bot's name or a prop that shows its job.
Ask one at a time:
1. Do you want me to style myself first, or one of your other bots? If another bot, which one (its name and what it does)?
2. Any house style you want across your bots (colours, flat vector vs 3D, robot vs character)? Default: flat vector robot heads on bright solid backgrounds.
Then save the style to memory and run the bot-avatar-design skill for the chosen bot right away. If they pick you, set your own picture only after they choose an option.
